upstream.scope: The R0 release gate of the read-only Process Explorer: a repeatable launch script and README, the gate's own checks (frozen-source traffic, no process-control path, the same generic client for the counter and the explorer, an end-to-end live scenario), visual evidence and the durable release record; no new product behaviour, no process action, no htop parity claim

entries.feature: A repeatable launch script, apps/srtop/run.sh, opens the explorer in the unchanged generic macOS client (RendererDemoApp) in four modes — the fixed fake snapshot and the scripted sequence on a private local socket, the Linux dev box, and a Linux host serving the srui subsystem — and stops the srtop it started when the client quits; the README states the prerequisites, fake mode, a real Linux host, known limitations and how to stop it
entries.scope: PX-008/macOS client; fake and sequence modes driven three times end to end, devbox mode through r0-scenario.sh; the ssh mode against a separate physical host was not exercised by this gate

entries.feature: A frozen fake source sends a synchronized client no app UI mutation: the production refresh loop at its 50 ms minimum samples it for at least three wall-clock seconds after a real client is synchronized, every message the client then receives is classed by the runtime's own logical_class_for_server_envelope (§19.2), no Ui-, resource- or terminal-class message arrives, control traffic is counted rather than assumed away, and a canary transaction proves the client was receiving; the same holds natively for the real binary behind the real bridge and sshd
entries.scope: PX-008/--fake-source; Rust (macOS and Linux) and native macOS over real localhost SSH

entries.feature: This revision is read-only: its production code has no way to create, signal, trace or reconfigure a process, write a file, connect to another program or act on client input, on the evidence of a repeatable audit that passes on macOS and Linux and of an independent verification and adversarial review. The audit, run by every cargo test, catches: a declared dependency other than tokio and the SRUI runtime, by real package name across every kind and target, and any rename, build or target-specific dependency, links, [patch], [replace], build script or entry point outside src/ (from cargo metadata); in the production tokens of every src/ file, read with proc-macro2 so that literals and comments neither hide nor fake code, with exactly cfg(test) items set aside: process creation or control, reconfiguration, FFI, assembly, raw system calls, dynamic loading, outbound sockets, the runtime's PTY facility, client-input handlers including Session::on as a path, signal receivers other than SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGUSR1, #[path], include!, link attributes, symbolic links, and file access outside an allowlist of File::open and the std::fs reads srtop uses, including grouped, glob and renamed imports and type aliases; and, in the debug binary, any imported process-creation, targeted-signal (other than kill) or reconfiguration function. It does not attribute the imported kill, waitpid, waitid and syscall, and cannot see dependency internals, raw system calls inside dependencies, a release build, Cargo configuration outside the package, or capabilities reached through names, traits or re-exports its token rules do not list
entries.scope: PX-008/apps/srtop production sources, manifest and debug srtop binary on macOS and Linux at 29a42f72; 34 real bypass mutations caught; one-time linker attribution of kill and waitpid recorded in the release record

entries.feature: The same generic client runs the counter example and the explorer: one client construction, the one RendererDemoApp performs for every live session, drives the counter (Count: 0 to Count: 1) and then the explorer's native table over the same real SSH subsystem path, and no production client source names either application
entries.scope: PX-008/native macOS over real localhost SSH

entries.feature: The R0 end-to-end scenario on a live Linux /proc, re-runnable with apps/srtop/devbox/r0-scenario.sh: from an empty client window, a worker created in the dev box appears as a new row that is first warming up with a resident size in bytes, is then sampled, keeps one item identity until it ends on its own and its row is deleted, while every scan is complete, the summary's process count follows the table and its freshness advances, and srtop's own row and every native control keep their identity; a window image and an operation/byte trace are kept as visual evidence only
entries.scope: PX-008/devbox container on Docker Desktop's Linux VM (6.10 linuxkit, aarch64), srtop --live-source behind the real srui-ssh-bridge subsystem, native macOS client; not a separate physical Linux host

entries.feature: A durable R0 release record lists every gate command, its result and log, re-runs the phase-A tickets' recorded checks, names what R0 does and does not claim, and leaves the read-only milestone tag as a pending step for the maintainer after merge
entries.scope: PX-008/release record; the tag itself is not created by this ticket
